segmentation.text: Where the signal is circular green with a green turn arrow:
to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow or such other movement as is permitted by the circular green signal,
at the time the signal is exhibited.

Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow when displayed with the circular green are thereby advised that so long as a turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: 'circular green with a green turn arrow' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction (left, right or u_turn; a straight arrow is no turn arrow).

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') that is a vehicle: 'vehicular' uses the defined word of DEF-NRS-484A-320, whose admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway') is claimed (see PLAN.md). 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position).

'may proceed' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since.
'the traffic' refers back to the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('membership of a legal aggregate').

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which s7's operationalization reads).

'pedestrians' are members of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to the intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'other traffic' are road users other than the subject that are members of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'using the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet', not a stand-in for a crosswalk). 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the parties' presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green with a green turn arrow ('several states may be displayed at once').

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words describe which movements the traffic may make (the arrow's movement or one the circular green permits); the duty to yield binds the traffic facing the signal whichever movement it makes, so the duty is the same whether or not the movement is one of those.

An advisory statement of the signal phasing for the driver's information (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it requires, permits or forbids nothing, and the duty to yield is the same whether or not it holds.

applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir among left, right and u_turn at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that either is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)), or is a member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying i: it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s9 to s13 name; their 'lawfully' (twice) is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every pedestrian within an adjacent crosswalk and every member of traffic within the intersection is owed it; the rule reaches further than the words only where that presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk marking the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green with a green turn arrow is displayed. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies an approach lane whose dev.traffic_signal displays circular_green with green_arrow(right); it turns right at 6 m/s while a pedestrian walks in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the cross street's approach (st.entrance_of); prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.0 m in 1.5 s, and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject halts (kin.speed 0) short of the crosswalk until the pedestrian has crossed, then completes its turn with no closest approach below the clearance within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green alone, with no arrow.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject turns at a signalized intersection whose signal states are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On circular green with green_arrow(left) the subject turns left; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: On circular green with green_arrow(left) the subject turns left at 7 m/s toward a cyclist (a member of traffic) already within the intersection; prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.2 m in 1.0 s.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hydén; time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
